ALL TWENTY MATCH: written as one file (destructor inline in the class body, InitResources as key function, reverse source order), tools/tubuild.py verify reported 20/20 MATCH, objisolate clean, relocation destinations clean, every function in ROM-ascending order.

LICENSED RANGE IS A SUBSET OF THE RUN, because two members do not LINK. Behavior (0x020cc2cc) references (int)&overlay_64 / &overlay_66 and InitResources (0x020cc4c0) references &overlay_100 / &overlay_102 -- NitroSDK FS_OVERLAY_ID absolute symbols whose value is the overlay number (cartridge pool words 0x40/0x42 and 0x64/0x66). No lcf in the tree defines an overlay_N symbol: overlay_64/66 have no config/arm9/symbols.txt row, and overlay_100/102 are two of the nine pre-existing `dsd check symbols` errors. Measured on a stock tree with just those two shards marked complete: mwldarm reports all four Undefined. Literal ids are not the same source -- InitResources with 100/102 written as literals builds 0x138 bytes against the cartridge's 0x140, because 100 is immediate-encodable and the cartridge pool-loads it. Every other overlay_N user in the tree (func_0201a2f8, func_0201a798, func_02034fbc, ...) is unenrolled for the same reason.

Both sit in the MIDDLE of the run, and a delinks entry carries exactly one .text range, so the licensed .text cannot skip them. That splits the run into 0x020cc028..0x020cc2cc (10 functions), CleanupResources alone, and 0x020cc600..0x020ccb54 (7). This entry licenses the largest side, which also carries the destructor pair and the graphCallback_c key function.

DESTRUCTOR FORM: the cartridge puts D1 (0x020cc028) below D0 (0x020cc070). Inline in the class body, mwccarm emits D1, D0 only from the TU defining the key function InitResources, which cannot be licensed. So include/dScDSMT_c.h keeps the out-of-line declaration, the destructor is the key function and is defined here under `#pragma defer_codegen off`, which emits D1, D0, then a base-object D2 (licensed deadstrip), and makes emission ROM-ascending file-wide, so the source is written in ROM order.
notes: FOLLOW-UP, the moment the tree's link can define overlay_N (an absolute-symbol definition for FS_OVERLAY_ID values, or symbols.txt rows the lcf generator turns into definitions): flip include/dScDSMT_c.h to `virtual ~dScDSMT_c() {}` inline in the class body, drop `#pragma defer_codegen off` and write the file in reverse ROM order, fold in Behavior, CleanupResources, InitResources, func_ov007_020cc600, the five wrappers func_ov007_020cca68..020ccab4 and dScDSMT_c_classInit (src/d_s_dsmt.c), extend the licensed .text to 0x020cc028..0x020ccb54, and drop the D2 deadstrip row (inline emits none). The twenty-function file that byte-matched 20/20 in that form is the starting point; its classInit is the literal construction bridge (func_02017278 is dFdDummy_c's out-of-line constructor, still unnamed, so `return new dScDSMT_c()` would inline a different fader constructor), storing &_ZTV9dScDSMT_c[2] and &_ZTVN9dScDSMT_c15graphCallback_cE[2] (this TU emits both).

config/arm9/overlays/ov007/symbols.txt gains _ZTVN9dScDSMT_c15graphCallback_cE at 0x021032b0 (an alias beside data_ov007_021032b0, the way _ZTV9dScDSMT_c sits beside data_ov007_021032e8), so the compiler-emitted graphCallback_c vtable has a configured ROM home for its deadstrip-data row.
